page: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the Tau T2D machine family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 60 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 60 vCPUs. It is equipped with 240 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the t2d-standard-60 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance. It also registers strong results in Geekbench multi-core testing and Passmark CPU benchmarks. Memory performance is mixed; while cached small-block read bandwidth is strong, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the average tier. Database operations, such as Redis SET operations and Passmark database tests, perform strongly, making the instance highly capable for transactional workloads. However, for large-scale AI tasks, such as text generation with a 70B parameter LLM, performance is weak, reflecting the lack of hardware acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2d-standard-60 offers a high density of dedicated physical cores without the overhead of hyperthreading, delivering predictable compute performance per resource unit. This makes it a viable option for multi-threaded workloads that require consistent CPU execution. Recommended workloads include multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, web serving, and moderate-scale data processing. It is less suitable for workloads requiring high-speed local NVMe storage or heavy parallel GPU computing.
description: Google Cloud Platform t2d-standard-60 is a general-purpose instance from the Tau T2D family, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 60 dedicated physical cores and 60 vCPUs. It features 240 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks highlight top-tier multi-core CPU capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core tests, alongside strong database and Redis execution. However, large-block memory bandwidth remains average, and large LLM text generation is weak due to the absence of hardware acceleration. This instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for compute-dense, non-hyperthreaded workloads, making it well-suited for multi-threaded software compilation, database hosting, and general-purpose enterprise applications.
